observation: TDD red-phase test discovery of CRITICAL async bug. Test suite proved the production async-empty-editor bug in multi-team path after initial implementation. Fixture masking was removed, loading gate added, async-path test written to drive the boundary condition. Green-phase implementation benefited from explicit lore comment (T1 constraint: TipTap captures initialContent once at mount, never re-syncs) and carry-forward architecture guidance. This is a textbook TDD + code-review collaboration that prevented a silent production bug.

Test-fixture masking of async boundaries. The fixture-fallback knowledgeFixtures in WorkBetCreate prevented the async-path bug from being caught in the test suite. The synchronous fixture-resolved test was too close to production for comfort but didn't exercise the real async boundary. Bug only manifested when real async data flow occurred (multi-team path). Emerging pattern: async-mocked services in tests need both happy-path and distinctly-async test cases.

Multi-team UX asymmetry under-specified at plan time. Architecture settled on reusing WorkBetCreate for multi-team, but user experience is visibly different: single-team is in-place+fast (MenuItem→POST→land), multi-team is page-nav+two-step (MenuItem→nav→team-select→Create). Both satisfy ACs functionally, but UX shape divergence should have been explicit in plan validation scenarios. When a feature has N distinct paths, each should have named test/scenario.

Explicit carry-forward lore comment + test verification proved effective. Reviewer called out 'this is the ONLY place sourceKnowledgeItemId can silently drop' with a tagged @lore AK5 comment in code. Builder explicitly carried it forward and tested it. Working pattern: single-point-of-failure spots should get explicit reviewer flagging + lore comment in place + test coverage. Prevention > discovery.

Stale forward-looking comment required doc follow-up commit. Initial implementation added 'defer to later' language in a comment describing the loading gate, but the feature was already implemented. Follow-up commit 9f7cd745 fixed the stale wording. Code-review should have flagged this as a NIT + auto-fixed in the same review round, not deferred to a separate doc commit.

Lore comments at decision points proved discoverable and valuable. Four @lore AK5 comments captured in code during implementation at the moment of architectural decision-making, indexed by workpackage + theme. Reviewer and builder both referenced these as rationale sources. Pattern is working. Future contributors can grep '@lore AK5' and find the architectural justifications.

Schema migration prose inaccurate; automation masked the error. Plan stated 'SQLite + Postgres both: ALTER TABLE bets ADD COLUMN ... REFERENCES ...' but codebase is Postgres-only and drizzle-kit emits ADD COLUMN + separate ADD CONSTRAINT FK, not inline REFERENCES. Plan also correctly said 'generated via npm run db:generate' — builder used automation so incorrect prose had zero impact on SQL. Lesson: hand-sketched DDL examples in plan prose are fragile; either dialect-explicit or omit.

AK1 harness-vocabulary rename incomplete in prose. Architecture prose referenced old deriveTitleFromPitch name (changed to deriveTitle in AK1). AK5 code is correct (reuses existing deriveTitle without server-side call); prose was out of sync with upstream rename. A vocabulary-sweep grep at plan-write time would have caught this. Plans should pin vocabulary to current code state, not assume historical names.

Code review CRITICAL → fix → re-review → DONE, one loop. Green-phase implementation shipped with empty-editor multi-team bug. Code review flagged CRITICAL. Builder immediately added loading gate + async-path test + removed fixture fallback. Re-review DONE. Total: one rework loop. Efficient recovery thanks to focused code-review CRITICAL flag and clear remediation path.

PR merge conflict in retro-log.jsonl: AK5 and AG7 retro entries appended to same file concurrently on separate branches. JSONL append conflicts are pure-append; resolution: keep both sets of entries. Root cause: concurrent WP pipelines writing to shared JSONL file without coordinated merge-base.
